mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our walk through Blake’s Selected Poems, think of these verses not as a roadmap, but as a true companion. They travel with you—through bright fields of innocence, into bustling streets of experience, across tangled woods of doubt, and out under the wide-open skies of imagination. Blake doesn’t hand out easy answers, but what he does offer is something just as valuable: a sense of company, courage, and real possibility. So, what’s worth carrying with you from all this? First, innocence—it’s not just about childhood. It’s a way of seeing the world, and you can return to it again and again. Experience? Sure, it brings its share of pain, but also opens the door to deeper understanding. Freedom doesn’t always come from grand gestures. Sometimes it shows up in those small, brave choices and in letting your imagination lead the way. Good and evil? They’re not set in stone. Wisdom grows when you’re willing to hold both together and listen for what they have to teach. And maybe most of all, art and connection—that’s how we make sense of it all, and that’s the legacy we leave behind. If you remember just one thing from Blake’s poems, let it be this: your questions matter. That ache for meaning, the longing to connect, those flashes of wonder—or even doubt—they’re not distractions. They’re the very heart of being alive. Blake reminds us we’re not alone in our searching. Every time you notice something beautiful, show a little kindness, or dare to create or reach out—you’re part of a bigger story. So keep asking. Keep imagining. Keep reaching for connection. The world’s deeper and stranger than it looks, and your voice—no matter how quiet or bold—belongs right there in the chorus. Take that with you, and see where it leads.
